info.name: image-resizer-goravel
info.description: Self-hosted image processing API (Goravel + govips/libvips). Upload a source image file + requested sizes, poll for the generated WebP outputs. See README.md for full API/config docs. Every "Create Image Request" call needs a local file picked for the "image" field - click it in Postman and use Select Files before sending.

variable.description: Set this to the "id" returned by a Create Image Request call, then use Get Image Request to poll it.

item.name: Resize modes
item.description: One request per resize mode, all using the same target box (400x400 or 400x200 where relevant) on the same uploaded image, so you can directly compare what each mode literally does to it.

item.name: Contain (fit) - fits inside the box, no crop, no stretch

request.description: contain (alias: fit): shrinks the whole image to fit entirely inside 400x400, preserving aspect ratio. Nothing is cropped and nothing is stretched - the result may come out smaller than the box on one axis (e.g. 400x268 for a landscape photo). Poll with Get Image Request and check the output's actual width/height: at most one of them will be 400.

item.name: Cover - fills the box, smart-crops the overflow

request.description: cover: fills the 400x400 box exactly (both dimensions always come out 400x400), cropping away whatever overflows - but the crop is biased toward the image's most visually 'interesting' region (faces/detail get kept in frame) rather than a plain center crop. Compare the output visually against "Crop" below on an off-center subject to see the difference.

item.name: Crop - fills the box, fixed center-crops the overflow

request.description: crop: fills the 400x400 box exactly, same as cover, but the crop is always a plain fixed center crop - no saliency/face detection. Cheaper and more predictable than cover, but can cut off an off-center subject that cover would have kept in frame.

item.name: Fill - stretches to the exact size (distorts aspect ratio)

request.description: fill: forces the image to exactly 400x200 regardless of its own aspect ratio. This is the ONLY mode that stretches/squashes the image - nothing is cropped, but circles become ellipses etc. Deliberately using a non-square 400x200 box here (rather than 400x400) makes the distortion obvious when you view the output.

item.name: Upscaling
item.description: Same source image, sizes both smaller and larger than it - showing what ALLOW_UPSCALE (server-wide, no per-request override) controls.

item.name: Upscale enabled (default) - large sizes actually enlarge

request.description: Upscaling follows the ALLOW_UPSCALE env default (true unless you changed it) - there is no per-request field for it. The 100x100 size shrinks normally; the 6000x6000 size will enlarge past the source image's own dimensions (check the response's "source_image" field vs the output's actual width/height). Set ALLOW_UPSCALE=false to see the 6000x6000 output capped at the source's size instead.

item.name: Size matrix - tiny to huge (8 sizes)

request.description: The same uploaded image run through 8 sizes from 10x10 up to 6000x6000. The small sizes exercise the downscale path; the sizes larger than the source image's own dimensions (check the response's "source_image" field) exercise the upscale path (enabled by default via ALLOW_UPSCALE). All use "contain" so only pure scaling is being compared, no cropping/stretching.

item.name: WebP quality
item.description: Same dimensions, different "quality" overrides - shows the filesize/fidelity tradeoff independent of resizing.

item.name: Quality comparison - low (10) vs default vs high (100)

request.description: Three identical 500x500 cover crops, differing only in WebP quality: 10 (visibly blocky, smallest file), the server default (IMAGE_DEFAULT_QUALITY, currently 80), and 100 (best fidelity, largest file). 0 and 100 are libvips' actual supported floor/ceiling (see IMAGE_QUALITY_MIN/MAX in .env.example) - quality is a pure encode-fidelity/filesize tradeoff, it never changes pixel dimensions. Poll and compare each output's file_size.
No "image" field at all. Expected: 422 with { "errors": { "image": [...] } }.
A file is attached but there's no "data" field. Expected: 422 with { "errors": { "data": [...] } }. Pick any local file for "image" before sending.
"mode" isn't one of contain/fit/cover/crop/fill. Expected: 422 with { "errors": { "sizes.0.mode": [...] } }.

Poll this until status is "completed" or "partially_completed". Each entry in "images" has a "url" (opens/renders inline in a browser) and a "download_url" (forces a browser download via Content-Disposition: attachment) for the generated WebP. Update the request_id collection variable to the id returned by whichever Create request you just ran.
